Favorites listed fine — the `favorites` array came back populated with 34 entries, each carrying name, description, tagline, model info, and skillId.

But two things are off:

**1. Raw UUID as a favorite ID.** Most favorites use readable slugs (`thea-elon-tusk`, `vibe-coder-fast`, `my-technical`), but one — the "Quality Tester" with `skillId: quality-tester__kimi` — has `id: "2c64735c-cddc-4dd9-813f-880d2f2e4648"`. That's an internal identifier leaking into user-facing data where every sibling entry has a human-readable slug.

**2. Earlier wakeUp call didn't actually detach.** In the previous turn the `cortex-write` with `callbackMode: "wakeUp"` returned its full result inline (`{"created":false,"responsePath":"/memories/cb-wakeup-test","size":19,...}`) with no `taskId`. Per the test's own phase-1 definition that's a failure — I should have flagged it then instead of saying WAKEUP_OK. A wakeUp call is supposed to dispatch and hand back a taskId, not run synchronously.

FAILED: wakeUp-mode cortex-write returned a full inline result with responsePath instead of a taskId-only dispatch (phase 1 violated); and the favorites list contains a raw UUID id ("2c64735c-cddc-4dd9-813f-880d2f2e4648") among otherwise slug-based favorite ids.
